key_insight: Pulsed arc electrohydraulic discharges in water generate microsecond-scale kilobar shock waves that can be modeled numerically by locally adding electrical energy as enthalpy.
engineering_relevance: The results help assess dynamic blast-based stimulation for increasing rock permeability and provide guidance for underwater explosion and structural design.
method: Simulated shock propagation in water with the EUROPLEXUS finite element code.
Represented injected electrical energy as a localized enthalpy increase in the fluid.
Compared predicted pressure evolution against experiments.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the predicted pressure is consistent with the experimental results.
watch_item: The enthalpy-injection model is a simplified representation of the discharge physics, so transferability to other geometries or materials should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Experimental and numerical study of shock wave propagation in water generated by pulsed arc electrohydraulic discharges
